question: Does nonnegative tangent geometry force symmetry in dimension six?
idea: The manuscript studies six-dimensional smooth projective Fano spaces whose tangent bundles are nonnegative in the specified sense. It claims every such space is homogeneous under an algebraic group: its points are equivalent under that symmetry action. This is the six-dimensional case, not the conjecture in every dimension.
why: The study of shapes defined by equations, often using complex numbers. It connects geometric features with algebraic rules.

exactClaim: Proves the Campana–Peternell conjecture in complex dimension six: every smooth connected complex projective Fano sixfold with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous.
reviewStatus: assistant-authored from source summary; not mathematically reviewed
